stem:
Meera's teacher brings a piece of granite rock to class. Meera says, "Rocks, minerals, and metals are all the same thing." Her friend Arjun explains the correct relationship and also tells her why rocks must be used carefully.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: Rocks are made up of metals, and rocks can be used without limits because they are visible everywhere.
Minerals are made up of rocks, and only rocks used for buildings need to be conserved.
Rocks are made up of minerals, metals such as iron and copper are extracted from minerals, and rocks form so slowly that they must be used responsibly.
Rocks, minerals, and metals are different names for the same thing, so there is no need to conserve them.

teacher.key_rationale: Rocks are composed of minerals; metals such as iron, copper, aluminium and gold are extracted from minerals. Rocks take thousands to millions of years to form, so they are effectively non-renewable and must be conserved and used responsibly. Option A wrongly says rocks are made of metals and implies unlimited use; B reverses the rock–mineral relationship and restricts conservation; D treats the three terms as interchangeable, the central misconception.
